The Legislature's own copy, one PDF per title (https://www.oklegislature.gov/OK_Statutes/CompleteTitles/os62.pdf: 2,798,279 bytes, 687 pages; os74.pdf: 5,271,337 bytes, 1,289 pages), was fetched and its text read: it is a whole title, dated December 2025 (the Legislature's index page says 'The Oklahoma Constitution and Oklahoma Statutes were last updated on November 18th, 2025'), and the shared code cannot take a range of it: src/check_seed_list.py accepts a `slice` only in the Colorado (article, part) and California shapes, so an Oklahoma title-PDF slice such as {section_start, section_end_before} fails the seed check. That is the one shared blocker: with such a shape the whole title file would be the snapshot (so the drift hash matches), the state module would cut the range in its to_text hook as Colorado does, and the seed check already allows one url under different slices (docs/research/oklahoma-statutes.md). The Legislature's December 2025 PDF predates the 2026 session amendments, so a slice would still need a currency check.

The url is the application's /Code page, whose shell is the same; the #fragment only keeps each seed url unique and is not a rule address. The Office documents no bulk file or API for the code's text (it offers monthly ZIP archives of only the rules changed that month, and annual Index of Changes spreadsheets). The number and title are copied from fetched bytes (cited by DTS Policies 1000-0003 and 5000-0002); the rule's text and current status could not be read.

The Legislature's PDF is a page scan (a full-page image on every page, about 300 ppi, per pdfimages) with a hidden text layer that is a machine reading and holds recognition errors, so it is not text of record (the layer opens with the noise ':,., ww,, a,,' and reads 'recogruzmg' for 'recognizing', 'Chieflnformation' for 'Chief Information' and 'ofDOA-DET' for 'of DOA-DET'). The corpus's two-engine OCR procedure (src/ingest_ocr.py) runs ocrmypdf without --force-ocr and so stops on any page that already has text (ingest run 2026-11-12: 'PriorOcrFoundError: page already has text!'); it needs a shared-code option to set the layer aside (Colorado's executive order stub met the same layer problem). Becomes a document when that option exists and the two engines clear the word and figure bars.

The Legislature's page for s. 16.61 serves a scrolling window of the chapter that stops inside the section: the page ends at s. 16.61 (5) (b), with no later subsection, no history line and a scroll-down control after it. The Fetcher bytes hold about half of the section (the Legislature's chapter 16 PDF, read for discovery, shows subs. The Wisconsin module refuses any statute page whose requested section runs to the end of the window without its history line (ingest run 2026-11-12).
